title: Sunday meal prep: how long leftovers last in the fridge
dek: If you are cooking for the week today, the USDA says leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Here is how to cool, store and reheat them safely.
keywords: how long do leftovers last in the fridge
keyPoints: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when it is above 90 degrees.
Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge and 3 to 4 months in the freezer.
Cool food quickly by dividing it into shallow containers.
Reheat to 165 degrees, measured with a food thermometer.

sources.title: Leftovers and Food Safety - USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

body: Sunday is a popular day to cook for the week. If that is your plan, it helps to know how long that food actually stays safe, especially in hot weather.

The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service says cooked leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator and 3 to 4 months in the freezer. That means a big batch made today is best eaten by Wednesday or Thursday. Anything you will not get to by then is better frozen right away in meal-sized portions.

Cooling matters as much as storage. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour if the temperature is above 90 degrees, which applies to a lot of California kitchens and patios this weekend. Divide large amounts into shallow containers so the food cools quickly and spends less time between 40 and 140 degrees, where bacteria grow fastest.

When it is time to eat, reheat leftovers to 165 degrees, checked with a food thermometer, and bring sauces and gravies to a rolling boil. For frozen meals, thawing in the refrigerator is the safest way; if you thaw in the microwave, reheat right away.
Labeling helps more than people expect. A strip of masking tape with the dish and the date takes seconds and removes the guessing later in the week.
Today's tip: plan your prep so the meals for Thursday and Friday go into the freezer, not the fridge.
